text:
When at the bottom you sleep, my dark beauty,

Of a vault worked in dark marble,

And you have no more for chamber and dwelling

Than a rain-soaked cave and a bony grave;


When the earth presses on your lazy flesh

And your flanks that idleness has charmingly polished,

And there is neither love nor heartbeat in your heart,

Nor can your feet go after anything,


The tomb, confidant of my infinite dream,

On those nights from which sleep is banished

—the tomb and the poet are sister and brother—


Will say to you: "Courtesan of uncertain charms,

What good is it now to have ignored the dead?"

Like remorse the worm will gnaw you.

translation.title: When at the Bottom You Sleep, My Dark Beauty
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the address to the dead beloved and the tomb's retaliatory speech.
